title: ASN event envelope
description: Canonical envelope carried by every ASN event. The broker validates this envelope and stores a content hash over the complete canonical serialization; per-event payload schemas constrain the payload object. See docs/decisions/0008-broker-transport-and-delivery-contract.md for the delivery contract.

event_id.description: UUIDv7 generated in the producing service's application code. Stable across outbox retries and broker redelivery; the broker treats a repeated event_id with identical content as a duplicate publish (200) and with differing content as a conflict (409).

type.description: Dotted lowercase event type, e.g. user.created or community.member_added. Breaking payload changes require a new type with a .v2 suffix per contracts/VERSIONING.md.

schema_version.description: Version of the payload schema for this event type. Additive changes keep the version; breaking changes publish a new event type.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC marking when the business change happened at the producer.

aggregate_type.description: Aggregate kind this event belongs to (e.g. user, conversation, community). Together with aggregate_id and aggregate_version; all three are present or all three are absent.

aggregate_id.description: Identifier of the aggregate instance. Soft reference to the owning service database (ref: <db>.<table>.<column>), never a foreign key.

aggregate_version.description: Strictly increasing, unique per (aggregate_type, aggregate_id). Exactly one event carries each version: this is a deliberate event-model constraint. The broker orders per-aggregate delivery by this value and rejects a reused version with 422.

trace_id.description: Optional correlation identifier (W3C trace id or UUID) propagated from the producing request.

payload.description: Event payload: identifiers and small deltas only. Large content travels by claim-check reference (an object-storage key), never inline. Payloads never contain plaintext chat content, private keys, recovery secrets, or raw backups. Constrained by the per-event schema for the event type.
